description: Collective-intelligence surveys — a named set of ideas someone is asked to choose between, and the response to it: the ideas chosen in priority order plus one new idea that was not in the set. The set is read from a JSON or CSV dataset by `ideas fetch "<url>"` when the program compiles; L0182 describes no flow and has no interactive player.

example_prompts.prompt: Set up the 'you-can-choose' survey from https://example.org/surveys/you-can-choose/ideas.json so I can record what I picked.
example_prompts.notes: The canonical starting point — `ideas fetch "<url>"` reads the set, and there is no response yet.

example_prompts.prompt: Create a survey from the team-priorities pool, titled 'Team Priorities', where you may pick at most 5.
example_prompts.notes: `title` and `max-choices` alongside the name. `max-choices` can never exceed the number of ideas.

example_prompts.prompt: Build the survey from that CSV of ideas, keeping the id column.
example_prompts.notes: `fetch` reads CSV as records keyed by the header row, so an `id,text` file gives ideas with their own ids. An entry with no id is numbered by position, i0 upward.

example_prompts.prompt: Record that I chose affordable housing, clean air and water, and voting rights, in that order.
example_prompts.notes: `selection` names the ideas chosen and the order is the ranking. An entry names an idea by its exact text, its id, or its position from 0. Use the text when the ideas were fetched — the set does not exist until the program compiles, so the ids cannot be known when the response is written.

example_prompts.prompt: Add my own idea alongside my selection: make public transit free.
example_prompts.notes: `idea` must not repeat one already in the set — that is what makes it new.

example_prompts.prompt: Record just a new idea — I do not want to pick any of the existing ones.
example_prompts.notes: `idea` may stand alone; `selection` comes back empty.
min-choices 2 max-choices 6. The compiler is the only thing enforcing these — there is no player.

example_prompts.prompt: Reorder my selection so the housing idea comes first.
example_prompts.notes: Reordering `selection` IS re-ranking; there is no separate rank step.
